scope: CBSE Class 6 Mathematics · Ganita Prakash · Chapter 4 · Data Handling and Presentation
claimBoundary: This is deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios. It is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, attainment claim, accessibility certification, or school-specific pacing validation.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 4 topic, a Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked required assessment type, a privacy-safe learner action, and an observable mastery criterion. Data-collection activities must use harmless synthetic or local paper examples, conclusions must remain bounded to the observed dataset, and graph/pictograph interpretation must use explicit keys, scales and baselines rather than visual impression alone.

scenarios.need: Learner treats a data value as its frequency, for example saying the frequency of value 4 is 4 even when 4 appears only three times.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: confusing a data value with its frequency
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use a short synthetic number list on paper, underline each occurrence of the target value, count those occurrences separately from the value itself, and label the result as frequency.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly distinguishes value from frequency in two new datasets and explains that frequency is the count of occurrences rather than the observed value.

scenarios.need: Learner loses or double-counts observations while converting an untidy raw list into tally marks and a frequency table.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Number each synthetic raw observation, cross it off exactly once while adding a tally, group tally marks in fives, then compare total frequency with the original observation count.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Builds two new tally/frequency tables with every observation counted exactly once and verifies that total frequency equals the raw observation count.

scenarios.need: Learner observes one category with the highest count and generalises the result to all Class 6 learners rather than limiting the conclusion to the sampled dataset.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: generalising a small dataset to everyone
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Read a small fictional frequency table and write two sentences: one statement supported by that dataset and one stronger population claim that the data do not justify.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: States a correct highest/lowest-frequency conclusion using bounded language such as 'in this dataset' and rejects an unsupported universal claim.

scenarios.need: Learner counts pictograph symbols as one item each even when the displayed key assigns several items to one symbol.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: assuming one symbol always means one item
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Box the pictograph key first, write 'number of symbols × value per symbol' beside each category, and convert every row into a numerical frequency before comparing categories.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly decodes two new pictographs with different keys and explains why symbol count alone is not the frequency when one symbol represents multiple items.

scenarios.need: Learner changes the pictograph key between rows or interprets a half-symbol without applying half of the stated full-symbol value.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use one written key for the whole pictograph, convert each full or allowed partial symbol numerically, then reconstruct the original frequency table as a reverse check without uploading any image.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Creates or verifies a new pictograph using one consistent key, handles an allowed half-symbol correctly, and reproduces every source frequency exactly.

scenarios.need: Learner reads the number of grid squares in a bar as the frequency even though each grid interval represents more than one unit.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: reading grid-square count as the frequency regardless of scale
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Write the numerical value of one equal grid interval beside the axis, calculate bar value as grid steps multiplied by scale, and check the result against a small source table.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Reads three new scaled bars correctly and constructs a bar height from a given frequency by applying one consistent numerical scale.

scenarios.need: Learner trusts dramatic visual differences between bars without checking that the graph uses a common baseline and equally spaced numerical intervals.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: trusting apparent bar size without checking axis labels
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare two paper graphs of the same synthetic values, inspect baseline and axis labels, calculate the actual numerical difference, and state which display gives the fairer visual comparison and why.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Identifies a truncated or inconsistent axis presentation in a new example and explains the distortion using the underlying numerical values rather than visual impression alone.

scenarios.need: Learner needs a fully offline route for data-handling practice and cannot depend on cloud charts, photo upload, microphone, camera, telemetry or remote teacher monitoring.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use cached Kiki text, locally rendered lesson content, a small fictional frequency table, paper and pencil to choose a scale and describe or draw a bar graph, with no network-dependent tutoring or submission step.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes the scale calculation, graph interpretation and mastery check using only offline local resources and gives a numerically correct explanation of the chosen scale and baseline.
